messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects observed on streaming-gateway in us-east-1. Error rate spike started ~10:05 UTC, affecting chunked streaming endpoints. Root thread: 2049991111

jen-oncall: Ack — I'm on it. Pulling up dashboards now. Can someone attach the SLO impact quickly?

anna-sre: Initial check — per-route 5xx for /v1/streams up to 18% over baseline. Latency P95 increased from 220ms to ~800ms. Affected customers: two high-volume tenants showing aborted streams (client-side sees ECONNRESET).

mike-runtime: Adding logs from gateway about client cancel / upstream reset. Seeing pattern where upstream model finishes but proxy closes early. Snippet:```
2026-03-15T10:07:12Z WARN gateway: upstream premature close: downstream chunked encoder failed: unexpected EOF
2026-03-15T10:07:12Z ERROR proxy: write failed: broken pipe
2026-03-15T10:07:13Z INFO request: client cancelled: connection reset by peer
```

maya-support: Two customers reported partial outputs and reconnect loops. One has a user-facing real-time chat; they saw ~40% of messages truncated in the window between 10:05-10:18 UTC. Ticket IDs: CUST-4532, CUST-4536.

zach-eng: I can repro locally with large token streams when proxy_buffer_size is small + chunked transfer. Repro steps: curl with chunked streaming -> gateway drops after ~8KB chunks. Example command:```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -d '{"stream":true, "prompt":"long-output"}' 
  https://gateway.internal/v1/streams
```
Observed: connection closed with HTTP/1.1 502 sometimes, or silent close.

anna-sre: Good catch. Hypothesis: proxy (nginx/envoy) hitting buffer or upstream connection close race with chunked encoder. Also seeing egress kernel-level resets on the nodes (~tcp_reset).

mike-runtime: Quick mitigation options:
- increase proxy_buffer_size / proxy_busy_buffers_size
- switch streaming route to websocket passthrough (bypass chunked encoding) for affected tenants
- enable temporary 10s prefix-caching for common prompts to reduce long tail
- divert traffic to dedicated capacity (redwood-dedicated-stream-2)
Which is fastest to flip?

jen-oncall: Priority order: 1) divert affected tenants to dedicated capacity (fast, per-tenant routing), 2) enable websocket passthrough for all streaming (risky but quick toggle), 3) increase buffers and roll config (safer but takes longer). I'll start routing for CUST-4532 and CUST-4536. @mike-runtime can you prepare the routing change?

mike-runtime: On it — creating canary route now. Command I'm using:```
rdwctl routes create --from tenant:CUST-4532 --to cluster:redwood-dedicated-stream-2 --reason "live mitigation streaming resets"
```
I'll mark it as canary for 5% then 100% if green.

maya-support: FYI customer comms: I'll send interim note to both tenants: "We're investigating streaming interruptions; temporary routing to dedicated capacity applied." Want wording approved.

anna-sre: Also adding temporary increased keepalive and tcp_retries for affected nodes. Patch:```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_retries2=8
```
This should reduce mid-stream TCP resets while we validate config.

qa-bot: Automated health checks show 5xx dropped from 18% to 4% for streams routed to redwood-dedicated-stream-2 after canary. Rolling to 100% for those tenants in 2m if no regressions.

mike-runtime: Canary completed and rolled. Monitoring shows successful stream completion rate for those tenants back to baseline. Gateway-level 5xx decreased by ~9 percentage points overall.

jen-oncall: Great. Next steps:
- Short-term mitigations applied (routing + keepalive).
- Medium-term: increase proxy buffer and evaluate websocket passthrough rollout to reduce chunked-encoding fragility.
- Long-term: implement robust chunked frame validation + retry at runtime to avoid partial frames causing upstream closes.
Assigning owners: anna-sre (postmortem + kernel/tcp investigation), mike-runtime (gateway config + websocket option), maya-support (customer comms), zach-eng (repro + test harness). I'll open the incident ticket and link to runbook.

jen-oncall: Creating incident: INC-20260315-001. ETA for mitigation validation: 30m. I'll stay on until postmortem opened. :thumbsup:

maya-support: Draft for customers: "We've applied a temporary routing change to reduce streaming interruptions and are monitoring. No data exposed; normal operations expected. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause once available." Approve?

anna-sre: Approve. Add note to include recommended retry guidance for SDKs (exponential backoff + reconnect).

zach-eng: I'll prepare a small integration test that simulates chunked frames with boundary sizes and random delays to catch this in CI. Putting a PR up: redwood/runtime#845.

mike-runtime: For on-call handoff — I'll add runbook steps I ran to avoid duplication. Path: /runbooks/streaming-chunked-mitigation.

jen-oncall: Thanks team. Leaving handoff to night oncall @jen-oncall -> @anna-sre for postmortem follow-up. If anyone sees new spikes re-open channel and ping :pager:.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-001 created by jen-oncall. Severity: Sev2. Links: https://internal.incidents/INC-20260315-001

(End of thread)
